# Where Kṣitigarbha works now: the myths behind the markets
Archetypes are not metaphors; they are job descriptions written early. **Kṣitigarbha**'s was unusually clear.

Kṣitigarbha's mythology is the story of a vow repeated across lifetimes — a brahmin daughter, a king — each life renewing the same impossible promise.

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) — which maps every flagship temple to the industries its archetype demonstrably resonates with, each match argued and open to challenge — seats this temple in **3 industries**. This file reads those seats the way they were earned: through the myths.
## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Kṣitigarbha
- **Pantheon:** Buddhist
- **Domain of influence:** Earth Womb, Savior of Hell Beings
- **Pattern seats:** 3
- **Sectors touched:** Society & Spirit · Culture & Entertainment · Home & Lifestyle
- **Strongest seat:** Funerary & Memorial Services
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 133 of 271
## The Myth at Work

**The Commission in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.** The Sūtra of the Past Vows of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva is set in the heaven of the Thirty-Three, where the Buddha preaches for his mother's sake before his passing.  There he recounts Kṣitigarbha's long record of vows and formally entrusts to him all beings of the coming age — the interval between Śākyamuni's parinirvāṇa and Maitreya's arrival. — hold that image; the industries below are where it goes to work.

**The Brahmin Daughter.** The sūtra's most beloved past life is a daughter's.  A pious brahmin girl's mother died slandering the Dharma, and the daughter, selling all she had to make offerings, was granted a vision of the Avīci hell — where she learned that her merit had already lifted her mother toward heaven. — remember the shape of that act. You will see it again, wearing a logo.
## The Seats

Each of these is argued in the atlas with a weight and a why-line. What the atlas cannot fit in one line is the whole myth — so here is each seat with its story restored.

### Funerary & Memorial Services

*Funeral care, memorials, and legacy services. (Sector: Society & Spirit)*

*The vow to empty the hells; the bodhisattva who attends the dead between lives.* Swap the costume and the sentence is indistinguishable from the myth. That is what a resonance seat means.

### Travel, Tourism & Place Branding

*Destinations, heritage tourism, and city branding. (Sector: Culture & Entertainment)*

*Protector of travelers on the roads of the six realms; the roadside guardian.* Swap the costume and the sentence is indistinguishable from the myth. That is what a resonance seat means.

### Wedding, Family & Maternity

*Weddings, childcare, and family services. (Sector: Home & Lifestyle)*

The why-line says it in one breath: *Guardian of children; as Jizō he watches over the young at every roadside.* That is not a resemblance; it is the same act, performed in a newer building.

Read the myth again after the seats and it stops sounding ancient: Kṣitigarbha's mythology is the story of a vow repeated across lifetimes — a brahmin daughter, a king — each life renewing the same impossible promise. The age changed. The work did not.
## The Method, Stated Plainly

None of this is numerology. A seat exists only where the match can be argued from the deity's documented domains and deeds — weighted, published, and falsifiable. The full derivation, the weights, and the challenge process are public on the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/). If a seat in this file reads wrong, the atlas itself tells you how to prove it — and the correction becomes part of the record.
## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in funerary & memorial services, travel, tourism & place branding, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/sites/ksitigarbha/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit. The story is the pitch; the seats are just where it already works.
